According to the FBI Vault listings on **vault.fbi.gov**, the following four subjects have a documented set of related files (the “parts”) that are listed on the site:

| Subject | Number of parts listed on the Vault |
|---------|------------------------------------|
| Mississippi Burning (MIBURN) | **9** (parts 01 – 09) |
| Highlander Folk School | **19** (parts 01 – 19) |
| Bayard Rustin | **7** (parts 01 – 07 (“Final”)) |
| Stokely Carmichael | **12** (parts 01 – 12 (“Final”)) |

**Which of them have more than 7 files?**  
Only the subjects whose part count exceeds 7 are:

- **Mississippi Burning (MIBURN)**
- **Highlander Folk School**
- **Stokely Carmichael**

*Bayard Rustin has exactly 7 parts, so it does not exceed the “more than 7” threshold.*

* Mississippi Burning (MIBURN) – the page lists “Part 01 … Part 09” (9 files).  
* Highlander Folk School – the page lists “Part 01 … Part 19” (19 files).  
* Bayard Rustin – the page lists “Part 01 … Part 07 (Final)” (7 files).  
* Stokely Carmichael – the page lists “Part 01 … Part 12 (Final)” (12 files).

**FBI Records : The Vault** (Federal Bureau of Investigation)
The Vault is FBI's FOIA Library, presenting ~7,000 documents scanned from paper for online viewing and PDF downloading. Many of the files listed below from commercial vendors are available here, at no charge.
**American Politics and Society from Kennedy to Watergate (1960-1975)**. (ProQuest History Vault.)
Includes:
*   **FBI Files on the American Indian Movement and Wounded Knee**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1967-1983. 139 folders (~26,000 pages).
Similar to the Archives Unbound collection. Includes published documents collected by the FBI concerning the Wounded Knee siege.
*   **FBI Files on the Weather Underground Organization**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1967-1976. 2 folders.
Includes profiles of WUO members and WUO publications, speeches, written statements, press releases, radio broadcast transcripts, interviews, and conference notes, with some SDS materials.
*   **FBI Files on White Extremist Organizations**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1934-1980. 93 folders.
Covers the KKK, American Nazi Party, and other white supremacy and anti-semitic groups. Include speeches, pamphlets, manuals, letters, memoranda, photographs, posters, interviews, circulars, newsletters, radio and television transcripts, and court documents.
**Archives Unbound** (Gale Cengage)
Includes:
*   **American Indian Movement and Native American radicalism**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1968-1979. 14,195 images.
Covers the evolution of AIM, including the 1972 "Trail of Broken Treaties" and the 1973 siege at Wounded Knee, South Dakota.
*   **FBI surveillance of James Forman and SNCC**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1961-1976. 43 folders (6,115 images).
Source: Special Collections and Archives, Benjamin S. Rosenthal Library, Queens College, City University of New York.

*   **Federal response to radicalism in the 1960s**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1956-1971. 602 folders (87,391 images).
Compiles independent subcollections:
• **COINTELPRO: The counterintelligence program of the FBI**. Covers CPUSA, New Left, Socialist Workers Party, White Hate Groups, Black Nationalist Hate Groups, Cuban Matters, Mexican Border Coverage, Puerto Rican Independence Groups, Yugoslav Emigres, Espionage, Hoodwink, Special Operations.
• **FBI file on Abbie Hoffman**.
• **FBI file on Cesar Chavez and the United Farm Workers**.
• **FBI file on the Brown Berets** (Los Boinas Cafes).
• **FBI file on the fire bombing and shooting at Kent State University**.
• **FBI File on the Students for a Democratic Society and the Weatherman Underground Organization**.
*   **Federal surveillance of African Americans, 1920-1984**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1920-1984. 1,293 folders (88,021 images).
Compiles independent subcollections:
• **FBI file : MIBURN (Mississippi Burning)**.
• **FBI file on A. Philip Randolph**.
• **FBI file on Adam Clayton Powell**.
• **FBI file on the Atlanta Child Murders (ATKID)**.
• **FBI file on the Black Panther Party, North Carolina**.
• **FBI file on the Committee for Public Justice**.
• **FBI file on Elijah Muhammed**.
• **FBI file on the Highlander Folk School**.
• **FBI file on the Ku Klux Klan murder of Viola Liuzzo**.
• **FBI file on Malcolm X**. NB. This supersedes other versions of this file.
• **FBI file on the Moorish Science Temple of America**.
• **FBI file on the murder of Lemuel Penn**.
• **FBI file on Muslim Mosque, Inc.**.
• **FBI file on the NAACP** [1923-1957].
• **FBI file on the National Negro Congress**.

• **FBI file on the Organization of Afro-American Unity (OAAU)**.
• **FBI file on Paul Robeson**.
• **FBI file on the Reverend Jesse Jackson**.
• **FBI file on Roy Wilkins**.
• **FBI file on the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee**.
• **FBI file on Thurgood Marshall**.
• **FBI file on W. E. B. Du Bois**.
• **FBI investigation file on Communist infiltration of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference**.
• **FBI investigation file on Marcus Garvey**.
*   **Federal surveillance of the Partido Independentista Puertorriqueño**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1941-1982. 46 folders (10.083 images).
Covers the Puerto Rican independence movement, including the PIP (founded in 1946). Includes files from US military intelligence agencies.
*   **Grassroots civil rights & social activism : FBI files on Benjamin J. Davis, Jr.**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1941-1990. 276 folders (71,934 images).
Source: Personal collection of Gerald Horne.
A broad range of topics are covered in this file on the African American member of the Communist Party USA, Harlem activist, and two-term New York City Councilman.
*   **The Hindu conspiracy cases : activities of the Indian Independence Movement in the U.S., 1908-1933**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1908-1933. 36 folders (2,796 images).
Covers Indian nationalists abetted by Germany in World War I. Mostly Immigration and Naturalization Service files and Justice Department files, including scattered Bureau of Investigation documents.
*   **Liberation movement in Africa and African America**This link opens in a new window
Date range: 1970-1985. 65 folders (11,513 images).
Covers the African Liberation Support Committee (ALSC) and All African People’s Revolutionary Party (A-APRP), two African American groups supporting the liberation struggles in Africa and Pan-Africanism. Includes State Department surveillance files on African Americans traveling to Africa.

byU.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)

This is a copy of Section 1 of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Headquarters file on Stokely Carmichael (Kwame Ture), 100-HQ-446080. The section ends in September of 1966, and does not include any of the other sections from this FBI file. Serials related to "JUNEMAIL," the FBI's program of installing wiretaps and bugs as part of its "electronic surveillance," have been removed from this document. It ends roughly one year before the FBI launched a counterintelligence program (COINTELPRO) against Carmichael in 1967.
A copy of this document may be found on the FBI's web site: http://vault.fbi.gov/Stokely%20Carmichael
Tens of thousands of pages from the FBI's many field office files on Carmichael are currently located at the National Archives: https://catalog.archives.gov/search?q=stokely%20fbi
